executive_summary.question: If a person intends to kill one individual but instead unintentionally causes the death of a different person, how is the resulting culpable homicide classified?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
Under the Indian Penal Code provisions reproduced in the retrieved text, when a person intends to kill (or knows his act is likely to cause death) one individual but, by that same act, unintentionally causes the death of another person, the resulting culpable homicide is **treated as if the intended victim had been killed**.  

Specifically, Section 102 states:

> “If a person, by doing anything which he intends or knows to be likely to cause death, commits culpable homicide by causing the death of any person, whose death he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause, the culpable homicide committed by the offender is of the description of which it would have been if he had caused the death of the person whose death he intended or knew himself to be likely to cause.”【ac6c1423-8651-4ff8-9f26-0cf720a5f981】

Thus, the culpable homicide is classified according to the mental state attached to the intended victim:

- If the act was done **with the intention of causing death** (or with the intention of causing bodily injury likely to cause death), it is **murder** (culpable homicide amounting to murder).  
- If the act was done **with the knowledge that it is likely to cause death but without any intention to cause death or such bodily injury**, it is **culpable homicide not amounting to murder** (subject to the punishments in Sections 103‑105).

In short, the unintended death is deemed to be of the same legal description as the death the offender intended or foresaw. If the intent was to kill, the offense is murder; if the intent was only to cause bodily injury likely to cause death, it is still murder; if there was merely knowledge of likely death without intent, it is culpable homicide not amounting to murder.  

*No further details about procedural defenses or exceptions are provided in the retrieved context.*
